display.purpose: The page title only, one per page, left-set; expanded 125% width, uppercase.

statement.purpose: Section headings at 112% width, sentence case; held to 13ch in the stage (12ch on landscape).

passage.purpose: A long passage set one phrase per line and grouped by sentence (lines on the line height, sentences 0.9em apart), in Chalk Ink; each phrase balances its own lines.

lead.purpose: The tagline, short answer lines under a statement and a closing contact line.

role.purpose: Titles inside hairline lists, at 106% width.

body.purpose: Supporting sentences in Ash Ink, held to 28-42ch.

label.purpose: The footer wordmark only, uppercase at 112% width; never a tag above a heading.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Everything that arrives or responds: press scale, arrow lean, the relief, stage and crease-map canvases and the still light fading in, the lamp's warm-up.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The hero lamp's one entrance sweep only.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.purpose: Colour, background and underline changes on hover, fine pointers only.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Primary button and quiet link while pressed.

motion.name: arrow-lean
motion.purpose: Arrows lean toward where they lead on hover.

motion.name: row-press
motion.purpose: Hairline list row while pressed.

motion.name: lamp-entrance
motion.purpose: Hero lamp sweeps once from left of centre to rest at upper right.

motion.name: lamp-warm
motion.purpose: Lamp intensity rises from dark to full during the entrance.

motion.name: lamp-spring-pointer
motion.purpose: Hero lamp follows a mouse pointer and returns to rest when it leaves. A pointer that arrives mid-entrance takes the lamp with its momentum: stiffness ramps in over 200ms, critically damped.

motion.name: relief-fade
motion.purpose: The hero relief, the stage canvas and the crease-map canvas appear only after their first frame, so they never pop in.

motion.name: still-light-fade
motion.purpose: The still lamp light fades in when the relief cannot run on a hardware GPU.

motion.name: glide
motion.purpose: Every scroll-scrubbed move and ramp in the stage; the page's strong ease-in-out would compress a move into a few frames under a scrub.

motion.name: scrub-spring
motion.purpose: The stage's timeline follows scroll position through it, so it plays backwards exactly as forwards; a jump lands directly.

motion.name: cut-dim
motion.value: relief falls dark over t 0.42-0.49; lamp eases to 40% over t 0.44-0.5 (glide)
motion.purpose: Scene A ends as one pool on black at about the brightness scene B opens with, so the cut matches in brightness as well as place and size.

motion.name: text-light
motion.value: on above 0.65 of its cue, off below 0.35; exponential ease, time constant 90ms in, 60ms out (about 300ms in, 200ms out)
motion.purpose: Stage text is lit and unlit in place as a state, never scrubbed or moved; it fades on every visible frame and lands on its state only off screen. Scene A's copy starts lit.

motion.name: held-lamp-spring
motion.purpose: The lamp a visitor leans or holds in the stage (moved only by a pointer that changes position), and the crease map's lamp and bend; the hero's own spring.

motion.name: touch-press
motion.value: a single still press of 400ms within 10px
motion.purpose: On touch, takes the stage's light on the subject; movement past 10px, a scroll or lifting the finger lets go.

motion.name: crease-pulse
motion.value: lamp-coloured crest at 75%, stroked 1.25x the crease width, +/-60px band, about 62% of the band width per second (340-900px/s), fade (1 - age/1.5)^1.35 over 1.5s; at most 3, a fourth retires the oldest over 150ms
motion.purpose: A click or still tap on the crease map (not a mouse or pen press on the words), and one pulse when the band's heading first comes into view.

motion.name: stage-edges
motion.value: top 10% fade while scrolling in; lower fade rising from 30% to 80% of the stage height by the time 35% of the stage has left
motion.purpose: The stage arrives out of the ground and sets into it.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No lamp sweep, no pointer following, no smooth scroll; the hero lamp sits at rest at full strength, the stage is plain sections and the crease map is still (also when switched on mid-visit).

narrative.overview:
The page is a matte graphite surface that absorbs light and shows only what one lamp chooses to reveal. On a hardware GPU the ground under the hero becomes a folded-plate relief, flat facets meeting at zigzag creases that run at ±30°, raked by a single neutral-warm lamp; below it the same lamp descends into one pinned stage, where it finds the approved images in the dark, and then into a band where the relief's creases return as hairlines. Without a GPU, a still pool of the same light, plain sections and a still crease map stand in. Either way the visitor meets a dark material first and an interface second.

The system is sparse and exact rather than dramatic. One family, Archivo, carries every word, and its width axis does the expressive work: expanded light capitals for the title, slightly widened light statements, normal width for reading. Ink is a tinted neutral in three steps. Content is separated by 1px hairlines and dark space, never by boxes, and the only solid fill on a screen is the primary button. Density is low: wide, fluid gaps of ground between subjects, short measures, nothing competing with the light.

Motion belongs to the light and to the reader's hand. The hero lamp sweeps in once and settles, then follows a mouse on a spring. In the stage, every move is a pure function of scroll position, scrubbed through a spring so it plays backwards exactly as forwards; scenes change by a cut on the lamp's pool, never through black, and a hand moving on the subject may lean or hold the light. Type never moves: it is lit or unlit. Nothing depends on motion, script or WebGL to be read. The system rejects the dark-tech default outright: a centred glowing headline over an orb or particle field, rows of glass cards, a neon accent, and the same fade-up on every section. Discretion is the brand's posture, so the visuals earn credibility through craft and never through claims.
keyCharacteristics: A matte graphite ground under a static 128px grain tile; never flat black.
One neutral-warm lamp, the only light; nothing else glows, and unlit areas fall to the ground, never below it.
A ±30° crease angle shared by the relief, its wall in the stage and the crease map.
Archivo alone; width (125, 112, 106, 100) is the expressive axis and weight stays light.
Hairlines instead of boxes, square corners, no UI shadows.
Scenes scrubbed by scroll, cut on the light, and answering only to a hand on the subject.
Complete and legible with motion reduced, scripts off or no GPU.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Light has one source and one colour. In every scene the lamp is the only thing that emits light; ink, hairlines, the button and the images reflect it and never glow.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Paint Rule
rules.body: The lamp colour appears only as light (the relief and its still stand-in, the stage's lamp, the crease map's lamp and pulses), as the focus ring and as the text selection. It is never a fill, a text colour, a border or an accent.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Text on the ground takes ink, ink-2 or ink-3 and nothing else: ink for what is read first, ink-2 for what supports it, ink-3 for fine print. The one inversion is the primary button, ground on ink. Interaction may raise ink-2 to ink; nothing changes hue.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo alone, from one variable file. Expression comes from the width axis, not from a second typeface: 125% for the title, 112% for statements, labels and controls, 106% for list titles, 100% for reading.

rules.name: The Light Type Rule
rules.body: Large type is light: 300 for the title and statements, 330 for the passage. Nothing is bold or italic; the heaviest weight in the system is the button's 560.

rules.name: The Still Type Rule
rules.body: Type never moves. Outside the stage every word is simply visible. In the stage each text block is lit or unlit as a state: it switches on at a point in the scroll and fades there in place (about 300ms in, 200ms out), never scrubbed and never resting half-lit. There is no translation, typing effect or split letters, every word is in the server HTML, and unlit text takes no pointer, so a selection never catches it.

rules.name: The Asymmetry Rule
rules.body: Content is left-set on asymmetric splits of the 12-column grid (5 and 7, or a 5-column heading over a passage stepped to columns 6 to 12); in the stage, copy holds the left column and the image the rest. Centring is kept for a short interlude: one statement, its lead lines and a narrow image, never a whole page.

rules.name: The Depth-Is-Light Rule
rules.body: Nothing is raised. Surfaces get depth only from the lamp falling across facets and images, from the lamp being occluded inside a lit scene, and from masks that let forms fall off into the ground.

rules.name: The Still Light Rule
rules.body: When the relief cannot run on a hardware GPU (a software WebGL renderer, no WebGL, or no script), a still radial pool of lamp light sits where the hero's lamp would rest. Content never depends on the relief.

rules.name: The Pixel Truth Rule
rules.body: Scenes draw only the approved images' own pixels. Light scales how much of a pixel shows and focus softens it; nothing adds surface, detail or geometry. Unlit areas fall to the ground colour, never below it.

rules.name: The Crease Angle Rule
rules.body: Folds and creases run at the relief's 30° angle and no other: the hero relief, the stage's wall and the crease map. Don't introduce skews, diagonal wipes or angled section edges.

rules.name: The No-Box Rule
rules.body: Content is never boxed: no cards, panels, outlined containers or framed images. Separation is a 1px hairline or dark space.

rules.name: The One Filled Control Rule
rules.body: The primary button is the only solid fill on a screen and appears once there; every other action is text with an arrow.

rules.name: The Brighten Rule
rules.body: Interaction only brightens: ink-2 rises to ink, a strong hairline to ink, ink to lit ink, and arrows lean 3px toward where they lead. Nothing changes hue, grows or lifts.

rules.name: The Scrub Rule
rules.body: Scenes are pure functions of scroll position, never of timers, and play backwards exactly as forwards. Only the text's on/off fade and the visitor's held lamp have time of their own.

rules.name: The Cut on the Light Rule
rules.body: A change of scene inside the stage is a match on the lamp's pool: the same place, size, scale and brightness on both sides, one pool on black, never a fade to black.

rules.name: The Hand on the Subject Rule
rules.body: The light answers only to a hand moving on the subject: moving on it leans the light, and in a hold takes it; moving off it lets go. A resting pointer, or a swipe, changes nothing.

dos: Do keep every surface on the graphite ground with its grain tile, and let the lamp (on the relief, in the stage, on the crease map, or as the still light) be the only thing that brightens it.
Do rest the lamp away from the type: in the hero it settles upper right while the title sits lower left; in the stage the copy holds the left column and the light works on the image to its right.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines (line, 12% ink) and dark space, and keep surfaces and controls square-cornered.
Do set every word in Archivo and change width before weight: 125% title; 112% statements, labels and controls; 106% list titles; 100% reading.
Do run any new fold or crease at the 30° crease angle.

Do ease arrivals and responses with cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), press controls to scale(0.97), and keep hover effects behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; ease scroll-scrubbed moves with cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1).
Do drive scenes from scroll position through a spring, so they play backwards exactly as forwards, and change scene on a match of the lamp's pool in place, size and brightness.

Do make every view complete without motion, script or WebGL: content visible by default, the still light in place of the relief, plain sections in place of the stage, the still crease map in place of the canvas.

Do use only approved images or abstract material, lit by the same lamp and falling off into the ground; draw only their own pixels, ship any derived raster with its provenance, and treat client originals in CSS only.
donts: Don't add glow, bloom or halos to type, controls, the mark or images; the only soft light is the lamp.
Don't use frosted glass, cards, panels or framed images.
Don't use gradients as decoration (gradient text, gradient buttons, tinted gradient backdrops); a gradient is only ever the lamp's falloff or a mask into the ground.
Don't introduce an accent colour, or use the lamp colour as paint.
Don't add box or drop shadows to the interface; the only shadows are the lamp's light occluded inside a lit scene.
Don't set a centred, glowing headline over an orb or particle field.
Don't move text into view, type it out or split it, or give every section the same entrance; in the stage text is lit in place, nowhere else does it animate.
Don't cut between scenes through black, or drive a scene from a timer.
Don't let a resting pointer or a swipe move the light; only a hand moving on the subject, or a still press on it, may.
Don't add surface, detail or geometry the approved images do not contain, or open the layered material wider than its own render.
Don't set anything bold or italic, or add a second typeface.
Don't add technical detail of the product or invented claims to any visual.
